question: Under the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations, after how many texting-while-driving convictions will a CMV driver's CDL be disqualified?
choice_a: One conviction
choice_b: Two or more convictions
choice_c: Three or more convictions
explanation: The manual states a CDL will be disqualified after two or more convictions of any state law on texting while operating a CMV, with 60 days for the second offense within 3 years and 120 days for three or more.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.9.5, Texting

question: At 55 mph, sending or reading a text message (which takes your eyes off the road for an average of 4.6 seconds) means you travel roughly how far without looking at the roadway?
choice_a: The length of an entire football field
choice_b: About 10 feet
choice_c: Half a car length
explanation: The manual states that at 55 mph you would travel 371 feet, or the length of an entire football field, without looking at the roadway while texting.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.9.5, Texting

question: According to the manual, how does a hands-free cell phone device compare to a hand-held device in terms of driver distraction?
choice_a: It is no less likely to cause distraction than a hand-held phone
choice_b: It eliminates distraction entirely
choice_c: It is legal only for hazmat-endorsed drivers
choice_d: It is required equipment on all CMVs
explanation: The manual notes that hands-free devices are no less likely than hand-held cell phones to cause distraction, because attention is diverted from driving while using either device.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.9, Cell Phones/Distracted Driving

question: If a driver reacts half a second slower because of distraction, what does the manual say happens to crash risk?
choice_a: It stays the same
choice_b: Crashes double
choice_c: It is cut in half
explanation: The manual states that if drivers react a half-second slower because of distractions, crashes double.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.9.6, Don't Drive Distracted

question: What is the key difference between aggressive driving and road rage as defined in the manual?
choice_a: Aggressive driving always involves intent to harm; road rage does not
choice_b: Road rage involves intent to do harm or physically assault another driver or vehicle, while aggressive driving is selfish, bold, or pushy driving without that intent
choice_c: They are legally identical terms with no distinction
choice_d: Aggressive driving applies only to commercial vehicles
explanation: The manual defines aggressive driving as operating a vehicle in a selfish, bold, or pushy manner without regard for others, while road rage is operating with intent to do harm or physically assault another driver or vehicle.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.10.1, What Is It?

question: What does the manual recommend if you are confronted by an aggressive driver?
choice_a: Speed up to hold your own in your travel lane
choice_b: Make every attempt to get out of their way and avoid eye contact
choice_c: Flash your high beams to warn them off
choice_d: Slow down in the left lane to block them
explanation: The manual advises making every attempt to get out of an aggressive driver's way, putting your pride aside, and avoiding eye contact.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.10.3, What You Should Do When Confronted by an Aggressive Driver

question: With low-beam headlights, about how far ahead can a driver typically see at night, according to the manual?
choice_a: 100 feet
choice_b: 250 feet
explanation: The manual states you can see ahead about 250 feet with low beams and about 350-500 feet with high beams.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.11.4, Vehicle Factors

question: According to the manual, within how many feet of an oncoming or followed vehicle should you dim your headlights?
choice_a: Within 100 feet
choice_b: Within 500 feet
choice_c: Only when the other driver flashes first
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to dim their lights within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle and when following another vehicle within 500 feet.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.11.5, Night Driving Procedures

question: Which of the following is listed in the manual as a warning sign of fatigue?
choice_a: Increased appetite
choice_b: Trouble remembering the last few miles driven
choice_c: Improved reaction time
explanation: The manual lists trouble remembering the last few miles driven, or missing exits or traffic signs, as a warning sign of fatigue.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.11.2, Driver Factors, Warning Signs of Fatigue

question: What does the manual recommend if you feel sleepy while driving and are not sure how tired you really are?
choice_a: Turn up the radio volume
choice_b: If you can safely do so, look at yourself in a mirror; if you look or feel sleepy, stop driving
choice_c: Roll down the window slightly and keep driving
choice_d: Drink coffee and continue to your destination
explanation: The manual advises looking at yourself in a mirror if safe to do so; if you look or feel sleepy, you are in a dangerous condition and the only safe cure is to sleep.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.11.5, Night Driving Procedures

question: According to the National Sleep Foundation's Sleep in America poll cited in the manual, what percentage of Americans have driven while feeling sleepy?
explanation: The manual cites the poll finding that 60% of Americans have driven while feeling sleepy.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.11.2, Driver Factors, Fatigue and Lack of Alertness

question: What is the manual's best advice for driving in fog?
choice_a: Use high beams for maximum visibility
choice_b: Don't -- pull off the road into a rest area or truck stop until visibility improves
choice_c: Follow closely behind another vehicle's taillights
choice_d: Maintain highway speed to clear the fog quickly
explanation: The manual states, "The best advice for driving in fog is don't. It is preferable that you pull off the road into a rest area or truck stop until visibility is better."
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.12, Driving in Fog

question: Which headlight setting does the manual recommend for best visibility when driving in fog, even in daytime?
choice_a: High beams
choice_b: Low-beam headlights and fog lights
choice_c: Parking lights only
choice_d: Hazard flashers in place of headlights
explanation: The manual recommends using low-beam headlights and fog lights for best visibility even in daytime, while being alert for drivers who forgot to turn their lights on.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.12, Driving in Fog

question: What is the minimum tread depth required in every major groove on front (steering) tires?
choice_a: 2/32 inch
choice_b: 4/32 inch
choice_c: 6/32 inch
explanation: The manual requires at least 4/32 inch tread depth in every major groove on front tires.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.13.1, Vehicle Checks, Tires

question: What is the minimum tread depth required on tires other than the front (steering) tires?
choice_a: 1/32 inch
choice_b: 2/32 inch
choice_c: 4/32 inch
explanation: The manual requires at least 2/32 inch tread depth on other tires (besides the front tires, which require 4/32 inch).
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.13.1, Vehicle Checks, Tires

question: Why does the manual say exhaust system leaks are especially dangerous in winter driving?
choice_a: They reduce fuel economy
choice_b: Poor cab ventilation with windows rolled up can let poisonous carbon monoxide leak into the vehicle
choice_c: They cause the engine to overheat immediately
explanation: The manual warns that loose exhaust connections can permit poisonous carbon monoxide to leak into the vehicle, which is especially dangerous when cab ventilation is poor, such as with windows rolled up.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.13.1, Vehicle Checks, Exhaust System

question: When crossing standing water or deep puddles, what does the manual recommend?
choice_a: Speed up quickly to clear the water
choice_b: Slow down, place the transmission in a low gear, and gently apply the brakes while crossing
choice_c: Shift into neutral and coast through
choice_d: Turn off the engine to avoid stalling
explanation: The manual advises slowing down, placing the transmission in a low gear, and gently applying the brakes to press linings against the drums or discs and keep water out.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.13.2, Driving, Wet Brakes

question: After driving through deep water, what should you do to your brakes before resuming normal speed?
choice_a: Nothing; they will dry automatically
choice_b: Maintain light pressure on the brakes for a short distance to heat them up and dry them out, then make a test stop
choice_c: Pump the parking brake ten times
choice_d: Pour water on the brake drums to cool them
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to maintain light brake pressure for a short distance to heat and dry the brakes, then make a test stop when safe to check that the brakes work well.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.13.2, Driving, Wet Brakes

question: A lack of spray from other vehicles ahead of you on a wet road most likely indicates what, per the manual?
choice_a: The road is well-drained
choice_b: Ice has formed on the road
choice_c: There is no traffic ahead
explanation: The manual states a lack of spray from other vehicles indicates ice has formed on the road, and advises also checking mirrors and wiper blades for ice.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.13.2, Driving, Check for Ice

question: In very hot weather, how often does the manual recommend inspecting your tires?
choice_a: Every 500 miles
choice_b: Every two hours or every 100 miles
choice_c: Once per day
explanation: The manual recommends inspecting the tires every two hours or every 100 miles when driving in very hot weather.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.14.1, Vehicle Checks, Tires

question: If a tire is too hot to touch during a stop in hot weather, what does the manual say to do?
choice_a: Let air out to reduce pressure
choice_b: Remain stopped until the tire cools off
choice_c: Pour water on it and continue driving
choice_d: Replace it immediately without inspecting the others
explanation: The manual instructs that if a tire is too hot to touch, you should remain stopped until it cools off, otherwise it may blow out or catch fire.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.14.1, Vehicle Checks, Tires

question: According to the manual, when should you never remove a radiator cap or any part of a pressurized cooling system?
choice_a: Anytime, it's always safe to do so
choice_b: Until the system has cooled
choice_c: Only while the engine is running
choice_d: Immediately after the engine overheats, to release pressure fast
explanation: The manual warns never to remove the radiator cap or any part of the pressurized system until it has cooled, since steam and boiling water can spray under pressure and cause severe burns.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.14.1, Vehicle Checks, Engine Coolant

question: What is a "passive" railroad-highway crossing, according to the manual?
choice_a: A crossing with flashing lights and gates
choice_b: A crossing with no traffic control device, where the decision to stop or proceed rests entirely with the driver
choice_c: A crossing used only by freight trains
choice_d: A crossing marked only with a stop sign
explanation: The manual defines a passive crossing as one without any type of traffic control device, requiring the driver to recognize the crossing, search for trains, and decide if it is safe to cross.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.15.1, Types of Crossings

question: If there is no white stop line painted on the pavement, how close to the nearest rail must a vehicle required to stop position itself?
choice_a: No closer than 5 feet and no farther than 20 feet
choice_b: No closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet
choice_c: Exactly 25 feet
choice_d: No closer than 50 feet and no farther than 100 feet
explanation: The manual states that without a white stop line, vehicles required to stop must stop no closer than 15 feet or more than 50 feet from the nearest rail.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.15.2, Warning Signs and Devices, Cross-buck Signs

question: About how long does it take a typical tractor-trailer unit to clear a single railroad track, per the manual?
choice_a: At least 5 seconds
choice_b: At least 14 seconds
choice_c: At least 30 seconds
explanation: The manual states it takes a typical tractor-trailer unit at least 14 seconds to clear a single track and more than 15 seconds to clear a double track.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.15.5, Crossing the Tracks

question: What should you do at a double railroad track after one train has cleared the crossing?
choice_a: Cross immediately since the visible track is clear
choice_b: Make sure no other train is approaching on the other track before crossing
choice_c: Wait exactly 60 seconds regardless of visibility
choice_d: Rely on the train's horn to warn you of a second train
explanation: The manual warns that a train on one track may hide a train on the other track, so after one train clears, be sure no other train is near before starting across.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.15.3, Driving Procedures, Double Tracks Require a Double Check

question: Which type of trailer does the manual specifically warn is at risk of getting stuck on raised railroad crossings?
choice_a: Refrigerated van trailers
choice_b: Low-slung units such as lowboys or car carriers
choice_c: Standard dry van trailers
explanation: The manual lists low-slung units (lowboy, car carrier, moving van, possum-belly livestock trailer) as being at risk of hanging up on raised railroad crossings.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.15.6, Special Situations

question: Why does the manual warn drivers not to rely on hearing a train's horn at a crossing?
choice_a: Trains are required to sound horns at every crossing, so this warning does not apply
choice_b: Trains may not, or are prohibited from, sounding horns at some crossings, and cab noise can also prevent you from hearing it
choice_c: Train horns are inaudible from any distance
choice_d: Horns are only used at night
explanation: The manual notes that trains may not sound horns at some crossings, and noise inside your vehicle may also prevent you from hearing the horn until the train is dangerously close.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.15.3, Driving Procedures, Don't Expect to Hear a Train

question: What should be the principal way of controlling your speed on a long, steep downgrade?
choice_a: Riding the brakes continuously
choice_b: The braking effect of the engine, using a low gear
choice_c: Shifting into neutral and coasting
choice_d: Intermittent use of the parking brake
explanation: The manual states you must use the braking effect of the engine, which is greatest in the lower gears near governed rpm, as the principal way of controlling speed, saving the brakes for when needed.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.16.1, Select a "Safe" Speed

question: Why should you select a low gear before starting down a grade, rather than trying to downshift after your speed has already built up?
choice_a: It saves fuel
choice_b: You may not be able to shift into a lower gear once speed has increased, and could lose all engine braking effect
choice_c: It is required only by state law, not federal law
explanation: The manual warns that if you don't downshift before your speed builds up, you may not be able to shift into a lower gear at all and could lose the engine braking effect.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.16.2, Select the Right Gear Before Starting Down the Grade

question: What happens to brakes that are used too much on a downgrade without relying on engine braking?
choice_a: They become more effective over time
choice_b: They can fade or fail from excessive heat
choice_c: They automatically self-adjust and improve
explanation: The manual explains that brakes can fade or fail from excessive heat caused by using them too much instead of relying on the engine braking effect.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.16.3, Brake Fading or Failure

question: What is an escape ramp designed to do?
choice_a: Provide a shortcut around mountain traffic
choice_b: Stop runaway vehicles safely without injuring drivers and passengers, using a bed of loose, soft material
choice_c: Allow vehicles to bypass weigh stations
choice_d: Provide overflow parking near steep grades
explanation: The manual describes escape ramps as built on steep downgrades to stop runaway vehicles safely, using a long bed of loose, soft material, sometimes combined with an upgrade.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.16.4, Proper Braking Technique

question: If you are forced to steer off the road onto the shoulder in an emergency, when does the manual say you should apply the brakes?
choice_a: Never brake at all while off the road
choice_b: Avoid braking until your speed has dropped to about 20 mph, then brake gently
choice_c: Brake as hard as possible immediately
explanation: The manual advises avoiding braking until your speed has dropped to about 20 mph, then braking very gently to avoid skidding on a loose surface.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.17.1, Steering to Avoid a Crash, Leaving the Road

question: In the "controlled braking" emergency stopping method, what should you do?
choice_a: Apply the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels, keeping steering movements small
choice_b: Pump the brakes rapidly on and off
choice_c: Apply the brakes fully and release only when the wheels lock, then reapply
explanation: The manual describes controlled braking as applying the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels while keeping steering movements very small.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.17.2, How to Stop Quickly and Safely, Controlled Braking

question: In the "stab braking" method, what should you do once the wheels lock up?
choice_a: Continue pressing the brake pedal harder
choice_b: Release the brakes, then reapply fully once the wheels start rolling again
choice_c: Pull the parking brake instead
explanation: The manual describes stab braking as releasing the brakes when the wheels lock, then reapplying fully once the wheels start rolling, noting it can take up to a second for wheels to start rolling again.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.17.2, How to Stop Quickly and Safely, Stab Braking

question: If a tire fails while you are driving, what does the manual say you should do regarding the brake?
choice_a: Brake hard immediately to stop as fast as possible
choice_b: Stay off the brake until the vehicle has slowed down, then brake very gently
choice_c: Pump the brakes rapidly
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to stay off the brake after a tire failure until the vehicle has slowed down, since braking could cause loss of control, and then brake very gently.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.17.4, Tire Failure

question: According to the manual, what are the two main causes of hydraulic brake failure?
choice_a: Overinflated tires and worn wiper blades
choice_b: Loss of hydraulic pressure and brake fade on long hills
choice_c: Faulty turn signals and dirty headlights
explanation: The manual states that most hydraulic brake failures occur from loss of hydraulic pressure or from brake fade on long hills.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.17.3, Brake Failure

question: What does ABS do, according to the manual?
choice_a: Decreases your normal braking capability
choice_b: Keeps your wheels from locking up during hard brake applications
choice_c: Increases your ultimate stopping power
choice_d: Replaces the need for regular brake maintenance
explanation: The manual describes ABS as a computerized system that keeps your wheels from locking up during hard brake applications, without decreasing or increasing your normal braking capability.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.18, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: The Department of Transportation requires ABS on truck tractors with air brakes built on or after what date?
choice_a: March 1, 1990
choice_b: March 1, 1997
choice_c: March 1, 2000
explanation: The manual states ABS is required on truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.18.2, Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

question: If your ABS malfunction lamp stays on after the bulb check, or comes on once you are underway, what should you do?
choice_a: Stop driving immediately, since ABS failure means you have no brakes at all
choice_b: Continue driving normally using your regular brakes, but get the system serviced soon
choice_c: Disconnect the trailer immediately
choice_d: Drive only in reverse until repaired
explanation: The manual explains that if the ABS malfunctions you still have regular brakes and should drive normally, but get the system serviced soon.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.18.7, Braking If ABS Is Not Working

question: According to the manual's ABS safety reminders, which statement is TRUE?
choice_a: ABS allows you to follow more closely
choice_b: ABS will always shorten your stopping distance
choice_c: ABS will not prevent skids caused by spinning the drive wheels or going too fast in a turn
choice_d: ABS replaces the need for regular brakes
explanation: The manual states ABS won't prevent power or turning skids -- it should prevent brake-induced skids or jackknifes, but not those caused by spinning the drive wheels or going too fast in a turn.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.18.8, Safety Reminders

question: Which of the following is listed in the manual as a cause of skids?
choice_a: Under-acceleration
choice_b: Over-braking, over-steering, over-acceleration, or driving too fast for conditions
choice_c: Using cruise control on a straight highway
explanation: The manual lists four causes of skids: over-braking, over-steering, over-acceleration, and driving too fast for road conditions.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.19, Skid Control and Recovery

question: What is the first thing you should do to correct a drive-wheel braking skid?
choice_a: Turn the steering wheel sharply in the opposite direction immediately
choice_b: Stop braking to let the rear wheels roll again
choice_c: Accelerate to regain traction
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to stop braking first, which lets the rear wheels roll again and keeps them from sliding, before counter-steering.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.19.2, Correcting a Drive-wheel Braking Skid

question: What causes most front-wheel skids, according to the manual?
choice_a: Overloaded rear axles
choice_b: Driving too fast for conditions
choice_c: Low engine RPM
choice_d: Excessive use of the parking brake
explanation: The manual states driving too fast for conditions causes most front-wheel skids, along with lack of tread on front tires or insufficient weight on the front axle.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.19.3, Front-wheel Skids

question: What are the three basic steps to take at any accident scene, according to the manual?
choice_a: Call your dispatcher, take photos, exchange insurance
choice_b: Protect the area, notify authorities, care for the injured
choice_c: Move all vehicles immediately, direct traffic, file a report
choice_d: Wait in your vehicle, call police, then leave the scene
explanation: The manual lists the basic accident procedure steps as protecting the area, notifying authorities, and caring for the injured.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.20, Accident Procedures

question: Why does the manual say you should NOT use water on an electrical fire?
choice_a: Water is too weak to be effective on any fire
choice_b: Water can cause electric shock
choice_c: Water spreads the flames of an electrical fire
explanation: The manual warns not to use water on an electrical fire because it can cause shock, and not to use water on a gasoline fire because it will spread the flames.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.21.3, Fire Fighting, Extinguish the Fire

question: When using a fire extinguisher on a vehicle fire, where should you aim it?
choice_a: Up into the flames
choice_b: At the source or base of the fire
choice_c: At the top of the smoke
explanation: The manual instructs aiming the extinguisher at the source or base of the fire, not up into the flames.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.21.3, Fire Fighting, Extinguish the Fire

question: With a cargo fire in a van or box trailer, especially one carrying hazardous materials, what does the manual say to do with the doors?
choice_a: Open them wide to let smoke escape
choice_b: Keep them shut, since opening them supplies oxygen and can cause the fire to burn very fast
choice_c: Remove them entirely
explanation: The manual instructs keeping the doors shut on a cargo fire in a van or box trailer, since opening them supplies oxygen and can cause the fire to burn very fast.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.21.3, Fire Fighting, Keep the Fire from Spreading

question: According to the manual, what is the only thing that will lower your Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC)?
choice_a: Drinking black coffee
choice_b: Taking a cold shower
choice_c: Time
explanation: The manual states the liver processes alcohol at a fixed rate, so only time -- not black coffee or a cold shower -- will sober you up.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.22.1, Alcohol and Driving, How Alcohol Works

question: About how much alcohol can the liver process per hour, according to the manual?
choice_a: One full standard drink
choice_b: One-third of an ounce
choice_c: Two full standard drinks
explanation: The manual states the liver can only process one-third an ounce of alcohol per hour, which is less than the alcohol in a standard drink.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.22.1, Alcohol and Driving, How Alcohol Works

question: According to the manual, when is possession and use of a drug prescribed by a doctor permitted for a CMV driver?
choice_a: Never, all drugs are prohibited regardless of prescription
choice_b: When the doctor informs the driver it will not affect safe driving ability
choice_c: Only if the driver is off duty for the entire trip
explanation: The manual states that possession and use of a drug given to a driver by a doctor is permitted if the doctor informs the driver it will not affect safe driving ability.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.22.2, Other Drugs

topic: Hazardous Materials Rules for All Drivers
question: What is required before a driver can operate a vehicle that requires hazardous materials placards?
choice_a: A valid CDL of any class
choice_b: A hazardous materials endorsement on the CDL
choice_c: A note from the employer only
explanation: The manual states you cannot drive a vehicle that requires placards unless your driver license has the hazardous materials endorsement.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.23.3, Lists of Regulated Products

topic: Hazardous Materials Rules for All Drivers
question: What are the four-digit identification numbers on hazmat placards or orange panels used for?
choice_a: To indicate the vehicle's registered weight
choice_b: A code used by first responders to identify the hazardous material, preceded by the letters "NA" or "UN"
choice_c: To show the driver's license number
explanation: The manual explains identification numbers are four-digit codes preceded by "NA" or "UN" used by first responders to identify hazardous materials, listed in the US DOT Emergency Response Guidebook.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.23.3, Lists of Regulated Products

topic: Hazardous Materials Rules for All Drivers
question: According to the manual, what is a tank endorsement required for?
choice_a: Any vehicle that carries dry bulk cargo
choice_b: A commercial vehicle designed to transport liquid or gaseous materials in a tank with an individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate capacity of 1,000 gallons or more
choice_c: Any vehicle over 10,000 pounds GVWR
choice_d: Only vehicles carrying hazardous liquids, never non-hazardous ones
explanation: The manual states a tank endorsement is required for a vehicle designed to transport liquid or gaseous material in a tank with individual capacity over 119 gallons and aggregate capacity of 1,000 gallons or more, whether or not the liquid or gas is hazardous.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.23.3, Lists of Regulated Products

topic: Hazardous Materials Rules for All Drivers
question: A placarded vehicle must have how many identical placards, and where are they positioned?
choice_a: Two placards, front and rear only
choice_b: At least four identical placards, on the front, rear, and both sides
choice_c: One placard on each rear door only
choice_d: Placards are only required on the trailer, never the tractor
explanation: The manual states a placarded vehicle must have at least four identical placards, placed on the front, rear, and both sides, readable from all four directions.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12; Iowa Department of Transportation) -- Section 2.23.3, Lists of Regulated Products
